newsitem.title: USA: Loral gets FCC ok to build CyberStar.
newsitem.headline: Loral gets FCC ok to build CyberStar.

text.p: Loral Space & Communications Ltd said on Monday that the U.S. Federal Communications Commission had granted the company a license to build and launch its CyberStar satellite-based digital communications system.

The $1.6 billion CyberStar system is a satellite-based digital telecommunications system designed to offer high-speed data and telecommunications services from leased Ku-band transponders satellites beginning in late 1997, Loral said in a statement.
CyberStar services will include low-cost Internet access, broadband interconnection, video-on-demand and other data services, the company said.

It anticipates that the services eventually will be delivered through a constellation of three interconnected geostationary satellites positioned over the Americas, Europe and the Middle East. The first of three CyberStar satellites is scheduled for launch and operation in 1999, the company said.
Space Systems/Loral, the designer of the CyberStar, will also provide the satellites, it added.
Loral Space & Communications Ltd., headquartered in New York, is a high-technology company that concentrates on satellite manufacturing and satellite-based services.
Loral recently announced an agreement to increase its ownership in Space Systems/Loral, its manufacturing unit, to 100 percent.
